newsitem.title: FINLAND: Clinton, Yeltsin summit ends, seen going well.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Yeltsin summit ends, seen going well.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin ended their summit on Friday and an American official said the talks had gone well.
"It just wrapped up," said one U.S. official. Another official said: "It is going very well." The two presidents are scheduled to hold a news conference at 1645 GMT.
Yeltsin's motorcade swept out of the grounds of Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari's official residence where the summit was held.

The two leaders spent only about 45 minutes in their afternoon session after a morning of talks lasting two and a half hours. Lunch talks on economic matters lasted about one hour, making a total of just over four hours of direct contact.

No further details on the talks were immediately available but U.S. officials have said statements on as many as five separate issues, including NATO-Russia relations and Russia's fledgling market economy, could be issued.

One U.S. official said the the U.S. negotiating team was now in a "pre-brief", a meeting where officials gather to assess the day's talks and to prepare for the news conference at the summit's close to be given by Yeltsin and Clinton.
A second U.S. official said the White House was operating on the assumption that the news conference would take place at 1645 GMT, as originally scheduled.
Officials rejected Finnish media reports that the summit had finished earlier than planned.
